A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CostBench and support a reliable comparison of the main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched; no material reading gaps remain.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of ten LLMs under static and dynamic conditions, sensitivity and robustness experiments, and human annotation validation.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main evaluation in Table 3, length-eight results in Table 4, and appendix robustness and annotation results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same task-generation pipeline, atomic/composite tools, cost assignment, interaction procedures, blocking mechanisms and ground-truth calculation. The runtime prompts in Figures 15-16 are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six travel-planning tasks and static/dynamic scenarios, including cost changes, tool bans, preference changes and composite-tool removal. No additional domain or task is evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the same ten LLMs and greedy baseline. Comparator membership in the length-eight experiment is also unchanged when v2 Table 9 becomes v3 Table 4.

E3.justification: The splits, 381-query filtered test set, task lengths, temperature 0, 16,384-token limit, 20-step tool limit, cost parameters, metrics and exclusion rules remain unchanged in Section 4.1 and Appendix B.

E4.justification: Cost-noise sensitivity, path coverage, repeated-blocking tests, seed robustness and failure-mode case studies are retained. The open-source/proprietary comparison and parameter-scaling observations moved into Section 4.2 already appeared in v2 Appendix D.4.

E5.justification: Both Appendix C.2 sections report 10,000 bootstrap resamples, 95% confidence intervals and additional experiments using seeds 1000, 2000 and 3000. The uncertainty table is renumbered from Table 8 to Table 9 without changing its reporting or values.

E6.justification: Table 3 values are identical, including GPT-5's 95.52% EMR. The relocated length-eight table preserves GPT-5's 74.79% and Gemini-2.5-Pro's 35.15% EMR. Plotted results, error statistics, confidence intervals and annotation-validation outcomes are also retained.

T1.justification: Appendix B retains the same tool-graph and metric definitions, shortest-path formulation, deterministic-generation equations and solvability proof, including the n-2 tool-ban robustness bound. Mathematical reflow does not change the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about a scalable cost-centric benchmark, dynamic replanning evaluation and weaknesses in current LLMs. The principal novelty and performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The generalization discussion drops the specific assertion of seamless adaptation to e-commerce, healthcare scheduling and logistics without changing core logic (v2 Appendix E versus v3 Section 6). This modestly trims applicability assertions; the broader easy-extension statement in Limitations and existing result interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a direct Hugging Face dataset link on the title page alongside the retained code-repository link, improving resource access information. Implementation descriptions, hyperparameters, prompts and annotation procedures are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including ToolR0, BiasBusters, PlanBenchXL, AdaPlanBench and work on sequential tasks, while removing Lin and Xu's Understanding Tool-Integrated Reasoning reference. These update supporting literature without substantially changing the benchmark comparisons or novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v3 moves Appendix D.4's findings into Section 4.2 and Appendix E's discussion into a main-text Section 6. Data Annotation becomes Appendix E. Wording, cross-references and author information receive limited edits; most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The existing length-eight results table moves from appendix Table 9 to main-text Table 4 in a more compact format. Other tables are renumbered, title-page resource icons are added, and surrounding layout reflows. Original figures and table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the hardest-task results and existing interpretive discussion easier to find in the main text, and adds an explicit dataset link. These provide limited gains in readability and resource discoverability. Experimental evidence, methods and substantive limitations remain essentially unchanged, so the revision does not resolve a major scientific deficiency.
